text:
Ava (runtime): heads-up — after the quant+attn-kernel rollout v2.3.1 we see a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate on prod: global hit 72% -> 40% across web tier, tail latency up ~18ms. logs attached below.
Diego: ugh. timeframe? what % rollout? :eyes:
Ava (runtime): rollout started 2026-03-15 03:10 UTC, ~35% of requests on dedicated pools. regression appeared ~03:25. sre-bot posted alerts for increased p95 token-latency and increased RPCs to model.
sre-bot: [alert] prefix_cache_hit_rate decreased from 0.72 to 0.40 (5m window) on cluster-us-east-1-dedicated-3. Incident link: https://incidents.internal/INC-20260315-01
Jun: can you paste the sample cache-key generation and logs? suspect key normalization drift between fp16 path and int8 path.
Ava (runtime): snippet from runtime key gen (simplified):
```
key = H("model:" + model_id + ":build:" + runtime_build_id + ":toknorm:" + normalize(prompt_tokens))
```
log example:
```
[03:24:59] user=svc-frontend req=0x7f8a model=redwood-open-1 build=20260310-kernelv2.3.1 path=quant_int8 key=3b9f... hit=false
[03:24:59] user=svc-frontend req=0x80a1 model=redwood-open-1 build=20260309-kernelv2.2.9 path=fp16 key=3b9f... hit=true
```
Maya: the keys look identical in hex prefix there but hit differs — could be subtle binary difference (padding byte, null terminator) or different tokenizer normalization (whitespace, NFKC).
Rory: we added an attention-optimization that uses a fused pre-pad op that left a trailing 0 byte in the serialized KV prefix for the quant kernel path. that would change H(...) even if printed hex prefix was same length.
Diego: can we reproduce locally by forcing quant kernel on a cluster and running the warmup prompt set? I can spin a dev pool.
Ava (runtime): repro steps I used: boot dedicated-dev-quant, set KERNEL_VARIANT=quant_int8, run warmup harness: tools/warmup/run.sh --prompts=prod-top-1k --batch=8. observed hit-rate 0.38 vs 0.74 on fp16 variant.
Jun: quick mitigation: add runtime fallback that canonicalizes keys (strip trailing nulls) + enable conservative kernel routing for 100% of traffic back to fp16 on critical customer routes. can we do that non-disruptively?
Ava (runtime): plan proposed: 1) roll routing to fp16 for the customer_critical route percentages (canary rollback automated), 2) instrument key bytes in metrics (expose kernel_variant label in prefix_cache_hit metric), 3) hotfix to key canonicalizer in runtime to normalize padding, 4) add unit + fuzz tests to ensure identical keying across kernel variants.
Maya: also check tokenizer commit bump last week — tokenization whitespace normalization changed in 2026-03-10; could be compounding. check prompt-normalizer git sha vs runtime build.
Rory: confirmed tokenizer SHA matched, so main diff is in fused pre-pad codepath. I'll push a small change to strip padding before hash and roll to dev.
Diego: rolling canary - switching 50% -> 0% quant variant on us-east dedicated now. watching.
sre-bot: [info] route change applied: quant_int8 -> 0% on cluster-us-east-1-dedicated-3 at 03:47:02 UTC.
Ava (runtime): after routing rollback (03:50) hit-rate recovered to ~71% in 5m window and latency normalized.
Jun: follow-ups: add kernel_variant tag to cache-hit metric, add a nightly regression test that asserts hit-rate >= 65% on prod-warmup corpus after any kernel/quant change, and add a changelog gating step for keying-affecting PRs.
Rory: PR for canonicalizer hotfix opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/6743 — small strip() before H() and new unit tests.
Maya: good triage. can we also run a fuzz harness over the serialized KV prefix to catch trailing zeros/hpack differences?
Diego: yep I'll add to warmup harness. will run it against next quant rollout in staging.
Ava (runtime): summary: regression caused by kernel-specific serialization difference introduced by fused pre-pad in quant path -> altered key bytes -> cache misswave. rollback to fp16 routing restored hit-rate. fixes: canonicalize key, add kernel-tagged metrics, add regression tests and fuzzing. leaving this thread open until PR merge + next rollout validation. :white_check_mark:
